newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse upside seen capped by primary offers.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse upside seen capped by primary offers.

text.p: Major forthcoming ticket primary offers are seen keeping the Warsaw bourse from posting gains next week but analysts saw Poland's strong fundamentals offering the market solid support and discouraging selling.
They said parliamentary elections, due in September, were also cooling demand, and analysts saw Warsaw's main WIG index locked in a horizontal trend between 16,000 and 17,000 points. @
"The situation may last and last, it doesn't look as if there is anything to change it, good news and bad news cancel each other out," said Kamil Kalemba, a trader at ING Baring Securities.
The WIG index eased 0.3 percent this week to 16,382.3 points on Friday. @

An offer of non-ferrous metals products maker Hutmen worth at 60-million zlotys began on Thursday and will continue next week while a privatisation offering of shares in Bank Handlowy kicks off on May 26. The treasury is offering 45 pct of the bank estimated by some to be worth a total of $1 billion to retail and institutional investors.
The flotation of minority stakes in copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz SA estimated to be worth another $2-3 billion is due to follow next month. @

The number of companies listed on the exchange will hit a hundred next week with chemical company Viscoplast starting bourse trade on parallel market on Tuesday and Bauma construction materials maker on Wednesday.
Pepees food producer shares will be alloted at a special bourse session on Monday.
Analysts said earnings reports for April, a bulk of them due on Monday, were unlikely to have an impact on the overall market. @
Banks, the bourse's heavyweights, rebounded slightly this week with BRE the top gainer with a 17.1 percent rise.

Analysts said, however, banks' earnings prospects for 1997 were weak, after an unspectacular first quarter and saw their current gains as only a reaction to a 30 percent drop in the last three months.
Analysts said a drop in year-on-year inflation to 15.3-percent in April, a figure reported on Thursday, was a good sign but they expected its impact on the market only in the longer-term. @
The second biggest gainer was Espebepe, which rose 15.3 percent on speculation before a May 16 creditors' meeting decides on a crucial debt write-off proposal.
The biggest losers were KPBP Bick, which fell 10 percent and Elektrim, which fell 9.4 percent.
